html:
Combine some of the stages, creating another giant cheat sheet

Given everything I have read, I can’t help but think that Piaget’s stages are very accurate (with the caveats that the stages are actually overlapping waves and that the exact ages/windows are actually distributional)

(1) action-bound, here-and-now control (sensorimotor), to (2) symbolic but egocentric and surface-driven representations (pre-operational), to (3) reversible operations over concrete relations and quantities (concrete operational), to (4) propositional, hypothetical, and combinatorial reasoning (formal operational).

If you were Jean Piaget, how would you train an AGI, purely in terms of the stages of training and the environments/data-engines?

https://gemini.google.com/share/7d0547775a87

Assuming you are a genius of developmental psychology, computational neuroscience, cognitive neuroscience, and modern machine learning, how would you train an AGI, purely in terms of the stages of training and the environments/data-engines?

Initialization (till birth)

Pre-Pre-Training (till  2)

Sensorimotor stage (Piaget divided it into 6 sub-stages, which probably hold up; see wikipedia page for Piaget’s theory)

Pre-Training (till  7)

Early Mid-Training (till  12)

Late Mid-Training (till  18)

Long-horizon exploration with heightened reward sensitivity and dopamine/frontostriatal remodeling

When we say concrete -> formal operational, what exact representations are present that were not present before?

Feature,Concrete Operational Representation,Formal Operational Representation Logic Type,"Class Logic: Hierarchy, inclusion (e.g., ""Are there more roses or flowers?"").",Propositional Logic: Relations between statements (p⟹q). Structure,"Groupings: Simple, localized clusters of rules.",Lattice / Group: A unified system where every part relates to the whole. Reality,Real -> Possible: Possibility is just an extension of what is real.,Possible -> Real: Reality is just one instance of the set of all possibilities.

Giant table; example columns: social (skills and learning algorithm as sub-columns), same for each domain, then neural

Scientific reasoning

The capability is innate/early, but the deployment of that capability across complex, abstract domains is what develops over time.

Early Childhood (3-5) Implicit & Contextual. "I know if I pull both levers, I don’t know which one worked." (Intuitive grasp of confounding).

Middle Childhood (6-10) Emerging Explicit. Can describe the strategy if prompted, but often reverts to "engineering mode" (trying to produce an effect rather than test a hypothesis).

Adolescence/Adult Explicit & Generalized. Can apply CVS to novel, complex, and abstract systems and understands why it is necessary for validity.
